About HarZa 
 HarZa is a team that has scaled e-commerce brands from zero to seven and nine figures. We build direct-to-consumer health and wellness brands for customers in the United States, and right now we are building Oralux, our oral health brand focused on gum health, alongside our at-home red light therapy line. We are around 150 people across more than 15 countries, fully remote, and we hold a high bar for accuracy in everything we say about health.
 The Role 
 We are building a small roster of licensed dentists and dermatologists to be the educational voice of our community. Our customers are mostly between 50 and 70. Many have tried products that promised a lot and delivered little, so they are skeptical, and they deserve straight answers from a real clinician. Your job is to give them those answers: what is happening with their gums or their skin, how the science behind light therapy and gum care actually works, what is realistic, and what they should ask their own doctor.
 This is an educational role, and we mean it. You will never appear in paid advertising, never endorse a product, never make product claims on camera and never diagnose or treat members. Our ads use actors. What we need from you is clinical knowledge, explained clearly, and a sharp eye on the accuracy of what our team publishes.
 What You'll Own 
 Live education. You host a recurring "Ask the Doctor" session for our member community on a weekly slot scheduled around your availability, answering questions submitted in advance about gum recession, gum health, skin aging and light therapy, always as general education.
 Educational content. You record short on-camera explainers from a content brief: how things work, common myths, honest expectations and what to ask your own doctor. Content is used in our community and organic channels, never in paid ads.
 Claims review. You review scripts, articles and landing pages in your specialty for medical accuracy before they go live, and when something overreaches you propose the accurate version rather than just rejecting it.
 A claims guide for your specialty. In your first two months you help us write down what we can and cannot say about gum health or light therapy, so the whole team works from the same line.
 Community answers. Between sessions you answer a handful of written member questions in the community, on your own schedule.
 What You Bring 
 An active, verifiable license as a dentist (DDS, DMD, BDS or equivalent) or as a dermatologist, in good standing with your regulator. Native or native-level spoken English, with the ability to explain clinical concepts to a non-technical 60 year old without jargon. Real comfort on camera, live and recorded, with a warm and steady presence. Working knowledge of periodontal health and gum recession, or of photobiomodulation, red and near-infrared light and age-related skin change, depending on your specialty. Clear judgment on the difference between education and claims. Reliability on a recurring weekly slot that we schedule around your availability, within US-friendly hours.
 Nice to Have 
 A periodontics or aesthetic dermatology background. Experience creating patient education content on YouTube, social, courses or webinars. Experience reviewing health marketing for accuracy, or working with consumer health brands.
 How We Work 
 We are remote-first and async-first. Day to day you work with our content and community team through shared Slack channels, from clear briefs and a written claims guide. Live collaboration happens within our window of 8am to 12pm Eastern Time, while your member sessions run on the weekly slot we agree with you. We plan around outcomes, not hours, and we expect people to come with a recommendation, not only a question.
 What You'll Walk Into 
 You will be one of several clinicians, so consistency with the roster and the claims guide matters more than any single voice. Our customers are skeptical and many of their questions repeat, which takes patience. Once your weekly slot is agreed, members count on it and notice when it moves. Reviews have real turnaround times because launches wait on them.
 What We Offer 
 A long-term, part-time engagement as an independent contractor with HarZa, with a rate of USD 100 to 200 per hour depending on experience and scope. Payment is monthly in USD: we send through Wise and you can receive in the USD account or wallet you already use. A small, serious team that cares about getting the science right, and a community of members who genuinely want to understand their health.
 Location 
 Remote. Native or native-level spoken English is required.
 How to Apply 
 Along with your CV, please share a link (unlisted YouTube, Loom or Google Drive) to a 60 to 90 second video in which you explain, as if speaking to a 60 year old patient, either why gums recede and what can and cannot be done about it, or what red light therapy actually does to the skin. No editing or production needed. We watch every video before scheduling a call.

We're transforming the grocery industry 
 Instacart is a Flex First team 
 Overview
 Every day, millions of people use Instacart to get the essentials they need, and along the way they discover new ways to save and earn rewards. Our payments, loyalty, offers and retailer storefront teams power those moments, with a mission to make affordability and financial ease accessible to all through experiences that feel seamless and rewarding.
 Instacart powers grocery shopping in two ways: the Instacart marketplace, where customers shop across many retailers in one app, and a white-label product that lets retailers run their own branded storefronts, loyalty programs and offers on our technology. This role sits on the team that designs the shared building blocks behind both, including offers, loyalty, payments and savings modules that retailers configure to create their own store experiences.
 Our customers face real financial pressure, and our retail partners need flexible ways to express their brands. As loyalty and white-label storefronts grow, we need stronger guardrails, configurations and governance so work done once can be reused with confidence across consumers, retailers and brands.
 This scope extends horizontally across both our primary marketplace and white-label solutions, flexing across workstreams while the work is still taking shape, then systemizing it: turning emerging patterns into well-crafted components, configurations and guidelines woven into product and tooling. The right candidate will work to ensure our retail partners and consumers have access to cutting-edge yet intuitive solutions for offers, discounts, loyalty programs.
 About the Job
 As a Senior Product Designer II on this platform, you’ll pair strong product judgment with deep craft in components and design language. Your focus is a kit of primitives and component foundations that deliver best-in-class experiences across loyalty, payments, savings and more, powering both the Instacart marketplace and the retailer storefronts built on our white-label offering. Through thoughtful design, you’ll bridge the gap between complex business goals and intuitive user experiences across offers to make the underlying system as thoughtful as the screens built on it.
 Day-to-day, you’ll work with a multidisciplinary team to identify the key moments across the funnel (for example, loyalty on Storefront home vs. the cart) and design components structured to assemble into cohesive, scalable experiences. You’ll balance the needs of customers (transparency and simplicity), retailers (business growth and customer loyalty), and brands (ad campaigns and conversions).
 Define the design language point of view for the retailer space: how storefronts, loyalty and offers express partner brands while staying consistent, accessible and trustworthy.
 Define configurable components that serve many surfaces and partners through set options rather than custom builds.
 Design the configuration layer that Professional Services, integrators and retailers use to set up components for their needs.
 Build first versions of experiences end-to-end, from discovery through delivery, including problem framing, exploration, prototyping, validation, and handoff.
 Flex across workstreams (loyalty, offers, retailer storefronts) while work is still taking shape, then systemize what you learn into patterns, components and guidelines.
 Use AI-enhanced tools to accelerate component exploration, prototyping, documentation and help the team adopt those practices.
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Research, Data Science and retail partners to shape requirements, and translate through clear storytelling and interactive prototypes.
